# Job Chapter 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 420v–421r

---

**1** "Look — I have seen all of this with my own eyes. I have heard it and understood it for myself.

**2** Everything you know, I know too. I am every bit your equal. **3** But it is the Almighty I want to speak to. I want to argue my case directly with God.

**4** You, on the other hand, smear everything with lies. You are all worthless doctors. **5** If only you would shut your mouths — that would be the wisest thing you could do!

**6** Listen to my argument. Pay attention to the case I am making. **7** Are you going to lie on God's behalf? Are you going to speak deceitfully to defend him? **8** Are you going to take his side no matter what? Are you going to play lawyer for God? **9** Would it go well for you if he examined you closely? Can you fool him the way you fool other people? **10** He would certainly rebuke you if he caught you secretly showing favoritism. **11** Wouldn't his majesty terrify you? Wouldn't the dread of him overwhelm you?

**12** Your grand arguments are worth no more than ashes. Your defenses crumble like clay.

**13** Be quiet and let me speak! Let whatever comes, come. **14** I will take my life in my hands — why not risk everything? **15** Even if he kills me, I will still hope in him — but I will defend my ways to his face!

**16** And this itself may be my deliverance, for no godless person would dare come before him. **17** Listen carefully to what I say. Let my declaration ring in your ears.

**18** I have prepared my legal case. I know that I will be vindicated. **19** Who can bring a charge against me? If someone can, I will be silent and accept death.

**20** Only two things I ask of you, God, and then I will not hide from you: **21** Take your heavy hand off me, and stop terrifying me with your dread.

**22** Then summon me and I will answer, or let me speak and you respond. **23** How many sins have I committed? Show me! Tell me what my transgression is!

**24** Why do you hide your face from me? Why do you treat me like your enemy? **25** Are you going to terrorize a windblown leaf? Are you going to chase down a piece of dry straw?

**26** You write bitter accusations against me and charge me with the sins of my youth. **27** You lock my feet in the stocks. You watch my every step. You mark the very soles of my feet.

**28** Meanwhile I waste away like something rotting, like a garment being eaten by moths."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The courtroom drama:** Job 13 is the most explicitly legal chapter in the book so far. Job uses courtroom language throughout: "argue my case" (v.3), "pleadings" (v.6), "show partiality" (v.8), "searches you out" (v.9), "prepared my case" (v.18), "contend with me" (v.19), "call and I will answer" (v.22). Job wants his day in court with God — not as a penitent sinner, but as a plaintiff demanding justice.

**"Though he slay me" (v.15):** This verse has carried the weight of centuries of devotion, but its meaning depends on a single Hebrew letter. The written text says "I have no hope" — raw despair. The traditional reading says "I will hope in him" — defiant faith. The genius of the ambiguity is that both are true simultaneously: Job has no hope AND he will not let go. That paradox is the beating heart of the book.

**Turning on God (vv.20-27):** Job transitions from addressing his friends to addressing God directly, and the shift is electric. His tone moves from legal argument to raw accusation: Why are you hiding? Why are you treating me as an enemy? Why are you terrorizing a leaf?

*— PNEUMA*
